experiment.name: Age group and death in B. rossi (S-CB050): dogs under 12 months against older dogs
experiment.description: Do dogs under 12 months die of B. rossi babesiosis more or less often than older dogs, and does sex change that? The package hypothesis is that age changes the form of severe disease more than the overall risk.

tests: A2 MH stratified by sex, permutation within sex
parameters.outcome: died, includes euthanasia for poor prognosis

experiment.summary: S-CB050: 6 of 50 dogs under 12 months died against 9 of 90 older dogs, odds ratio 1.23 (95% CI 0.34 to 4.15, Fisher p 0.778); sex-stratified MH OR 1.24 (0.41 to 3.77). Only an OR of about 3.7 or more (or 0.28 or less) was detectable. 0 of 3 tests q < 0.05.

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Do dogs under 12 months die of B. rossi babesiosis more or less often than older dogs? This is step 1 of SV-05, whose hypothesis is that age changes the form of severe disease (anaemia in young dogs, inflammation in adults) more than it changes the risk of death.

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: S-CB050 (Onderstepoort, SRC-A) has 141 infected dogs, 1 without an age: 50 under 12 months and 90 older. Death (which includes euthanasia for poor prognosis) by age group was tested with Fisher's exact test (A1), then stratified by sex with a Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio and a permutation test within sex (A2), and age in months was compared between dogs that died and survived (A3). Benjamini-Hochberg over the 3 tests. The spec was frozen before the outcome file was opened, but the age medians by outcome had been seen, so this step is exploratory.

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: 6 of 50 young dogs (12%) and 9 of 90 adults (10%) died: odds ratio 1.23 (95% CI 0.34 to 4.15), p 0.778. Within sex: females 1.97 (0.20 to 25.91), males 0.94 (0.15 to 4.54); pooled 1.24 (0.41 to 3.77), p 0.785. Dogs that died were not older: median 29 against 20 months, Hodges-Lehmann difference -1 months (-8 to +17), Cliff's delta -0.04 (-0.39 to +0.31). 0 of 3 tests pass q < 0.05. Death by sex (secondary): 10 of 93 males, 5 of 47 females, OR 1.01 (0.29 to 4.02).

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: It does not show that age has no effect on risk: with 15 deaths only an odds ratio of about 3.7 or more (or 0.28 or less) was detectable. One source only; age stands in for prior exposure, breed and size, which are not recorded, and neuter status is not in the file. The 'died' label includes euthanasia for poor prognosis, which can depend on cost and owner decisions.
